**Finding submitted: MISSING** (confidence 0.86)

**What I checked:** A full-text search for "insurance" returned no hits, and I read the complete General Provisions section (10.1 Notices through 10.8 Headings/Counterparts) plus the opening responsibilities section to confirm the gap is real rather than a mislabelled heading.

**Why it matters here:** HDI is squarely a services/hosting vendor under this deal — it designs, develops, operates and maintains the Site (§1.1), bears all technology and labor costs (§1.2), and hosts the Site on its own server (§1.3). Section 8.1 expressly contemplates that HDI "may have access to or be exposed to, directly or indirectly, Content, user information, data" of the Company. That places HDI in the playbook's walk-away category: a vendor that processes personal data with no insurance obligation at all. There is also no indemnification provision in the agreement, so insurance is the only backstop available to us for a hosting failure or data incident.

**The redline:** A new Section 10.9 inserted after paragraph p0070, at the preferred position — CGL USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber/privacy USD 5M tied expressly to HDI's hosting and data processing, workers' compensation as required by law, and certificates on request. The term runs through the agreement plus one year, matching the model language. The comment flags the E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M fallback so the negotiation has somewhere to land without a second round trip.

One drafting note worth passing to the deal team: the agreement already contains two provisions numbered 10.7 (Survival and Entire Agreement), so the numbering after 10.6 is off by one. I used 10.9 to sit cleanly after the existing 10.8, but if the numbering is corrected in a clean-up pass the insurance section should be renumbered to follow. Separately, §10.7 (Survival) lists Sections 6.3, 7, 9 and 10 as surviving for two years — since the new clause sits in Section 10, it inherits that survival period, which is consistent with (and slightly longer than) the one-year tail in the inserted language.
